title: Entanglement, anti-flatness, and nonlocal nonstabilizerness: a unified perspective from entanglement spectrum
abstract: Entanglement and nonstabilizerness capture distinct aspects of quantum complexity, yet their relation through the entanglement spectrum remains only partially understood. Here we develop a unified spectral framework for bipartite nonlocal nonstabilizerness. We introduce a generalized anti-flatness and derive universal upper and lower bounds on the nonlocal stabilizer Rényi entropy (SRE) in terms of Rényi entanglement entropy and spectral non-uniformity. We apply these bounds to exponentially and algebraically decaying spectra, revealing distinct relations between entanglement and nonlocal nonstabilizerness. For the marginal algebraic spectrum and the Calabrese--Lefevre spectrum, we further introduce a dyadic-shell sandwich construction that bounds the ordered entanglement spectrum by upper and lower shell-flat spectra and determines the asymptotic nonlocal SRE scaling. At one-dimensional conformal critical points, this yields a universal hierarchy of double-logarithmic scaling laws. Our spectral bounds and dyadic-shell sandwich construction provide general tools for analyzing nonlocal SRE, offering a flexible framework that can be applied to a wide range of entanglement spectra in quantum many-body systems.
summary: This theoretical paper unifies the study of entanglement and nonlocal nonstabilizerness by developing a spectral framework based on the entanglement spectrum. It derives universal bounds for the nonlocal stabilizer Rényi entropy using generalized anti-flatness. The framework successfully predicts distinct scaling laws for various spectral types, offering a general tool for analyzing quantum correlations in many-body systems.
main_problem: The paper aims to develop a unified spectral framework to understand the relationship between entanglement, anti-flatness, and nonlocal nonstabilizerness in quantum many-body systems.
main_result: The nonlocal SRE is shown to be controlled by complementary spectral structures derived from the entanglement spectrum, yielding universal scaling laws, such as double-logarithmic growth at 1D conformal critical points.
method: The authors derive universal upper and lower bounds on the nonlocal stabilizer Rényi entropy using generalized anti-flatness and introduce a 'dyadic-shell sandwich construction' to bound the ordered entanglement spectrum.
model_or_system: The analysis focuses on bipartite pure states in quantum many-body systems, specifically examining spectra that decay exponentially or algebraically, including the Calabrese--Lefevre spectrum relevant to 1D critical points.
key_observables: Nonlocal $\alpha$-Rényi Entropy ($	ext{M}_{	ext{NL}}^{\alpha}$), $\alpha$-Rényi Entanglement Entropy ($	ext{S}_{\alpha}$), and Generalized Anti-flatness ($\mathcal{A}_{\alpha}$)
important_parameters: The decay exponent $p$ in algebraic spectra, the entanglement parameter $\alpha$, and the system size $N$ or length $L$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the properties of the entanglement spectrum and the applicability of spectral bounding techniques like the dyadic-shell sandwich construction.
figures_summary: The notes mention schematic illustrations of the sandwich construction and results comparing the asymptotic scaling of $S_2$, $A_2$, and $M_{NL}^2$ for different decay regimes ($p>1, p=1, p \in(0, 1)$).
paper_structure: The paper develops the spectral framework by introducing bounds relating $	ext{M}_{	ext{NL}}^{\alpha}$ to $	ext{S}_{\alpha}$ and $\mathcal{A}_{\alpha}$. It then applies this framework to specific spectral types (exponential, algebraic, C-L) to derive concrete scaling laws and demonstrate the general applicability of the spectral tools.
why_interesting: This work provides powerful, general spectral tools to characterize complex non-local correlations (nonstabilizerness) in critical quantum systems, linking it rigorously to measurable quantities like entanglement entropy.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. (a) Schematic illustration of the shell-based sandwich construction. Within each dyadic shell Sj, the largest and smallest eigenvalues are used to construct upper and lower shell-flat spectra, respectively, which bound the original ordered ES from above and below. (b) Monte Carlo results for the algebraically decaying spectrum at p = 1, with L = log2 N. The fitted slope is 2.736 ± 0.017, approaching the asymptotic value 3. (c) Monte Carlo results for the C-L spectrum, with fitted slope 1.413 ± 0.020, approaching the predicted value 3/2.
